claim: Southport Pier has been closed since December 2022 and repair works are expected to begin in early 2026, taking approximately 14 months — so it will be closed throughout a May 2026 visit.
quote: the iconic Southport Pier...has sadly been closed since December 2022 for health and safety reasons. Repair and refurbishment works to Southport Pier are expected to get underway in early 2026. Once they start the works will take approximately fourteen months to complete

claim: A £20m UK Government Growth Mission Fund award unlocked the full restoration of the Grade II-listed Southport Pier in 2026.
quote: A full restoration of the unsafe structure, which has been closed since December 2022 for health and safety reasons, will now take place thanks to a £20 million investment from the UK Government's Growth Mission Fund.

claim: Southport's Victorian Botanic Gardens north of the centre have an 1874 glasshouse, lake and flowerbeds; nearby Hesketh Park (Edward Kemp, 1860s) sits at the north end of Lord Street with themed gardens, fountains and a lake.
quote: The Victorian Botanic Gardens is a calm pocket just north of the town centre with paths around the lake, colourful flowerbeds and an ornate glasshouse dating back to 1874

claim: Hesketh Park is a Victorian public park designed by Edward Kemp in the mid-19th century, situated near the north end of Lord Street.
quote: Hesketh Park is a public park situated near the north end of Lord Street in the Victorian seaside town of Southport... designed as a public park in the mid-19th century by Edward Kemp.

claim: Southport is hosting its first-ever Year of Culture in 2026 with major headline events including Lightport (Feb), the Big Top Festival (May) and Books Alive! (Oct), making 2026 an unusually rich year to visit.
quote: 2026 marks a standout year for Southport as it hosts its first-ever Year of Culture... Lightport – An immersive light and sound installation (14-16 February), Big Top Festival featuring world-leading circus performers (2-3 May), and Books Alive!

claim: Southport Pleasureland has been rebranded as Adventure Coast Southport, with free park entry and weekend/school-holiday operation 11am–5pm; rides are paid via a £36 unlimited wristband or a £2 top-up Fun Card.
quote: The park is open every weekend and daily during school holidays from 11am – 5pm... Entry to the park is now completely free... Unlimited Access Wristbands are priced at £36... or a Fun Card is available for just £2 per person

claim: Southport's 140-acre Marine Lake offers boating, pedalos, motor boats and landscaped promenade walks, originally built in the 19th century as a low-tide haven for vessels.
quote: Southport Marine Lake is a 140 acre purpose built lake which was originally constructed in the 19th century... With its shimmering waters, beautiful landscaped promenades and lush gardens, the Marine Lake is perfect for leisurely walks, picnics, and boating activities.

claim: The Atkinson in Southport is currently free to enter and runs the '20 Years of Another Place' photography exhibition (Ron Davies' shots of the Gormley figures) — a thematic tie-in for visitors combining Southport culture with a Crosby Beach trip.
quote: stunning photographs of Crosby beach's Iron Men, taken over two decades by Crosby photographer Ron Davies, are on display at The Atkinson in Southport

claim: Crosby Beach's 'Another Place' consists of 100 cast-iron, life-size Gormley body-casts spread across 3 km of foreshore and almost 1 km out to sea — each 189 cm tall and ~650 kg.
quote: Another Place consists of 100 cast-iron, life-size figures spread out along three kilometres of the foreshore, stretching almost one kilometre out to sea. The figures are cast replicas of Gormley's own body. Each figure is 189 centimeters tall and weighs about 650 kilograms.

claim: Crosby is a non-bathing beach with soft sand, mud and tide risk; visitors must stay within 50 m of the promenade and time visits to low tide.
quote: Crosby beach is a non-bathing beach with areas of soft sand and mud and a risk of changing tides. Visitors should stay within 50 metres of the promenade at all times and not attempt to walk out to the furthest figures.

claim: Formby sits within the North Merseyside/West Lancashire red squirrel stronghold — one of only a few UK refuges — with pine woods backing onto the dunes and beach.
quote: Formby is located within the North Merseyside and West Lancashire red squirrel stronghold, one of a few refuges left for red squirrels across the UK

claim: Formby's Victoria Road car park and toilets are closed until spring 2026 for a major conservation project, so visitors must use the Lifeboat Road entrance (free Blue Badge spaces) or arrive by train.
quote: Formby beach car park and toilets at Victoria Road are closed until spring 2026 for a major conservation project... the Lifeboat Road car park is the main option for parking.

claim: Formby Beach is dog-friendly year-round with no seasonal ban, but dogs must be leashed near the dunes to protect natterjacks and ground-nesting birds.
quote: Dogs are welcome year-round with no seasonal restrictions on the beach itself. However, dogs must be kept on a lead, especially near the dunes where wildlife protection is crucial.

claim: Ainsdale Sand Dunes NNR is one of the best remaining UK strongholds of the rare natterjack toad, with the Sefton Coast holding ~40% of the UK population.
quote: Ainsdale Sand Dunes National Nature Reserve is one of the best remaining strongholds of the rare natterjack toad, Europe's loudest amphibian. The Sefton Coast is home to 40% of the UK's population of rare natterjack toads.

claim: Late April is the best time at Ainsdale to hear the male natterjack toad's chorus — known locally as the 'Birkdale Nightingale' — from the flooded dune slacks.
quote: At night in late April the rare and endangered natterjack toad calls from around the fringes of the flooded slacks. The rare Natterjack Toad's astonishing chorus earns it the local name of 'Birkdale Nightingale'.

claim: Aughton to Southport is roughly 11 miles / ~17 minutes by car — comfortably within a 30 km radius of Moor Hall.
quote: The driving distance between Aughton to Southport is 11 miles. It takes approximately 17 minutes to drive from Aughton to Southport.

claim: Lytham St Annes is ~30 miles / 29.7 mi by road from Ormskirk (Aughton sits next door), pushing it well over a 30 km radius — borderline-out for this trip.
quote: The distance between Lytham St Annes and Ormskirk is 30 miles, with a road distance of 29.7 miles.

claim: The £73m+ Marine Lake Events Centre (1,200-seat theatre, 2,400-capacity conference space) is under construction with main works expected to start later in 2026, meaning visitors will see hoardings around part of the lakefront.
quote: the Marine Lake Events Centre will boast a 1,200-seat theatre, 2,400-capacity conference centre, and various offices, food and beverage offering, meeting rooms, and production facilities. Main construction works are expected to begin on site later in 2026
